title: Lesson 1: Expressing Opinions and Agreeing/Disagreeing
content: Grammar: Expressing opinions with phrases like 'I believe', 'In my opinion', and using modals like 'should', 'must'
Vocabulary: opinion, agree, disagree, perspective, suggest, recommend
Conversation: 'In my opinion, we should start the project earlier.' 'I see your point, but I think we need more time to prepare.'

exercises.question: Which sentence expresses an opinion?
options: I believe we need more team members.
exercises.answer: I believe we need more team members.

exercises.question: In my ________, we should wait until next week.
Match the phrase with its meaning
I ________ we should focus on marketing more.
What is a polite way to disagree?
options: I see your point, but I disagree.
exercises.answer: I see your point, but I disagree.

title: Lesson 2: Talking About Hypothetical Situations
content: Grammar: Second Conditional (If I were you, I would…)
Vocabulary: hypothetical, situation, consequence, unlikely, imagine
Conversation: 'If I were the manager, I would reduce working hours.' 'That would definitely improve morale!'

exercises.question: Which sentence uses the second conditional?
options: If I go there, I’ll call you.
If I were rich, I would travel the world.
If it rains, we’ll stay home.
If you see him, tell him I called.
exercises.answer: If I were rich, I would travel the world.

exercises.question: If I ______ you, I would accept the offer.
Match the clause with its result
She would be surprised if he _______ (arrive) early.
Which is a correct hypothetical sentence?
options: If I am taller, I play basketball.
If I have time, I go shopping.
If I were a bird, I would fly.
If he will come, we will start.
exercises.answer: If I were a bird, I would fly.

title: Lesson 3: Using Reported Speech
content: Grammar: Reported Speech (He said he was tired)
Vocabulary: report, mention, claim, explain, announce
Conversation: 'She said she would be late.' 'Did she mention why?'

exercises.question: What is the reported form of: 'I am hungry'?
He said he _______ (not know) the answer.
Match direct speech to reported speech

pairs.I will call you: He said he would call me

exercises.question: They said they _______ (leave) at 6 PM.
Which word is commonly used in reported speech?

title: Lesson 4: Talking About Past Habits
content: Grammar: Used to / Would for past habits
Vocabulary: habit, routine, childhood, regularly, previously
Conversation: 'I used to go fishing with my grandfather.' 'Same here! We would fish every weekend!'

exercises.question: Which sentence shows a past habit?
options: I go to the gym every day.
I used to play tennis after school.
exercises.answer: I used to play tennis after school.

exercises.question: When I was a kid, we _______ (go) to the beach every summer.
Match the phrase to its time reference
My father _______ tell stories before bed.
Which is NOT a past habit?
options: She used to sing in a band.
He would walk to school every day.
They used to travel a lot.

title: Lesson 5: Making Complaints and Apologies
content: Grammar: Modal verbs for politeness (could, would), formal structures for complaints
Vocabulary: complaint, apologize, issue, unacceptable, inconvenience
Conversation: 'I’d like to make a complaint about the noise.' 'We apologize for the inconvenience.'

exercises.question: Which is a polite way to complain?
options: I’d like to make a complaint.
exercises.answer: I’d like to make a complaint.

exercises.question: We _______ for the delay in service.
Match the phrase with the purpose
The food was cold. This is totally _______.
Which is a formal phrase to apologize?
